name: prompt-mode
description: `freecode -p "<prompt>"` runs one headless turn and prints ONLY the final response to stdout. This is the contract an LLM caller depends on: the answer is capturable with $(...), so the tool transcript that a normal session prints (the 'read(...)' call line, its result preview, the step divider) must not reach stdout, and neither must the model's mid-turn preamble. The turn still really runs tools - the fixture's step 1 calls read and step 2 answers from it - and stdoutAbsent proves the chrome went nowhere rather than that the tool never ran. Read-only is asserted where it actually matters, on what the model was offered: read/grep/list_dir present, create/edit/shell_exec/spawn_agent absent, with no approval prompt anywhere in the run
prompt: what does the package say its name is
